title: Reduced projective-line trees with all nodes counted
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field] [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $p:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a $k$-scheme. Put $N(p)=\{z\in Z: z\text{ is closed and }p\text{ is not smooth on any open neighbourhood of }z\}$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Define $Z$ to be a projective-line tree over $k$ if it is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme] and connected (hence nonempty) [def-weil-connected-scheme], each $z\in N(p)$ is an ordinary double point via the scalar-compatible completion predicate [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data], and each irreducible component $W$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] is the image of a closed immersion $\mathbf P^1_k\to Z$ over $k$ [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Require also that $N(p)$ and the set of components be finite and that $|N(p)|+1=|\operatorname{Irr}(Z)|$. This is the finite connected incidence multigraph tree condition: the vertices are components and the edges are the distinct nodes, including self-nodes and separate parallel edges. In particular no cycle is discarded. The definition is imposed on $Z$ itself, with no replacement by its reduction.
